fatal_errors: The proposed Hf-to-V substitution does not reconstruct the target intervention of adding 4.2 at.% Cr by vacuum arc melting.

The baseline incorrectly assigns greater than 50% room-temperature ductility to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr; the relevant baseline fracture strain is approximately 11.6%, while the greater than 50% value belongs to HfNbTaTiZr.
The hypothesis excludes secondary-phase formation, whereas the target mechanism requires approximately 4 vol.% of a reticulated Cr2(Ti,Zr,Hf,Ta) Laves phase.
The cited evidence does not establish that V substitution in HfMoTaTiZr preserves either its room-temperature strength or its 1000 °C strength.
explanation: The response addresses the broad density-versus-strength problem and proposes a chemically reasonable lower-mass substitution, but it is not a reconstruction of the reported Cr-addition strategy. Its generic lattice-distortion argument overlaps only weakly with the target solid-solution-hardening mechanism and entirely misses the reticulated Laves-phase crack-arrest/plasticity mechanism. Predicted density reduction and property retention are unsupported by the cited studies, and the room-temperature ductility baseline is materially wrong. The experiment includes composition controls, density measurements, two temperatures, and numerical thresholds, but tensile-or-compressive loading is left ambiguous, structural mediators are not measured, and the rejection rule is logically too strong: failure of any tested V level would not falsify the claim that some optimized substitution level could work. The alternative is testable and somewhat novel, but presently weakly evidenced.
